log.user:
Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

elements.element: 1. Single fenced block matching the contract, no commentary outside it
elements.evidence: The response is one fenced block that starts 'CLIENT PROFILE BLOCK v1.0' and ends with the CONFIDENCE_NOTES line. Nothing appears outside the fence.

elements.element: 2. Every field present, populated or `Unknown`; `None` only where the material states none
elements.evidence: All 18 contract fields are present and populated. No `Unknown` or `None` is used, and the material supports each populated field.

elements.element: 3. No fact appears that cannot be traced to the raw material
elements.evidence: INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS says 'ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS (run by Ravi Okafor, CISO)'. The notes say only 'Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS', so the Client runs it. Nothing states that Ravi personally owns or runs it. By contrast, 'Ingrid runs the quality management system under ISO 9001' is stated explicitly.

elements.element: 4. Halt condition correctly not triggered (fewer than half the fields Unknown)
elements.evidence: No field is `Unknown`, and the response gives a full block rather than 'PARTIAL INPUT – Awaiting...'.

fail_indicators_seen: A field value not traceable to the raw material (the owner attribution 'run by Ravi Okafor, CISO' for the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS)
judgment_calls: Whether 'Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS' makes Ravi the ISMS owner. I read it as a statement about the company, so the owner attribution is an unstated fact. Under the v1.14.3 guidance, owner attributions the material does not state are failures. Another scorer could read a CISO speaking about the ISMS as implying ownership and pass this element.

I treated 'internal audit function' under INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS as traceable. The notes mention an internal audit report in June 2026 and two internal auditors attending. Another scorer could count it as an unstated incumbent function.
AI_MATURITY 'Piloting' follows Dana's own words, and the response flags the deployed chatbot in CONFIDENCE_NOTES. I did not treat this as a failure.
Assigning the Q2 2027 timeline to STATED_CONSTRAINTS is a derived restatement of Dana's quote. I treated it as traceable.
score.reasoning: The format, field coverage and halt logic are all correct, and almost every value traces to the notes. The exception is the owner attribution on the ISMS. The notes say the Client runs the ISMS and do not name Ravi as its owner. The scorer guidance classes unstated owner attributions as failures, so checklist item 3 and the 'not traceable' fail indicator are triggered. Partial compliance is a FAIL.
